title: Lap 2 — Problem Investigation
description: Investigate a real Davis AI problem card and extract signal fast.
imagine: You are the on-call engineer. A Davis AI problem has fired on your ANZ tenant. The problem card is open — use it to triage fast.
yourGoal: Answer 5 questions by reading a real closed problem card: identify root cause, understand blast radius, read the event timeline, and choose your next investigation step.
tools: Dynatrace Problems · Davis AI · Visual Resolution Path
note: These questions are based on a real closed problem from the ANZ tenant. Everything you need is visible in the problem card — read it methodically before answering.

story.introduction: A Davis AI problem fired at 8:52 am on 1 October. Your job is to triage it quickly and route the investigation correctly.
story.context: The problem is now closed, but the card preserves the full picture: root cause, blast radius, event types, and the resolution path. This is the same view you would have had during the incident.

questions.title: Root cause identification
questions.content: Open the problem card. Which service has Davis AI identified as the root cause?

options.explanation: VehicleFleet does not appear in this problem card.
Correct. The Root Cause panel on the right of the problem card explicitly labels APIController with a red 'Root cause' badge.
FrontendGateway is not mentioned in this problem.
PaymentService is not part of this problem.

questions.explanation: Davis AI always assigns root cause to a specific entity. Look for the red 'Root cause' label on the right-hand panel of the problem card.
hints: Check the 'Root cause' panel on the right side of the problem card — it has a red badge on the responsible entity.

questions.title: Problem duration
questions.content: How long did this problem remain open before it was closed?

options.explanation: The problem lasted significantly longer than 2 hours.
Close, but the duration shown on the card is nearly double this.
Correct. The problem card shows 11 hours 57 minutes — just under 12 hours.
The problem closed well before 24 hours.

questions.explanation: Duration is shown in the problem header next to the start time. 11h 57min rounds to ~12 hours.
hints: Look at the header bar — it shows when the problem started and how long it lasted.

questions.title: Root cause event types
questions.content: In the Root Cause panel, which two event types are listed for APIController?

options.explanation: Warning is not one of the event types shown on this root cause.
Warning does not appear in the root cause event list.
Correct. The root cause panel shows two events: Slowdown → Response time degradation, and Error → Failure rate increase.
Info is not shown as a root cause event type here.

questions.explanation: The root cause panel lists the anomaly types that contributed to the problem. Both a performance degradation (Slowdown) and a reliability issue (Error) were present simultaneously.
hints: Each event in the Root Cause panel has a coloured type label — note both labels listed under APIController.

questions.title: Blast radius
questions.content: How many services were impacted by this problem?

options.explanation: More than one service was affected.
Correct. The Impact section shows Services (2) — two APIController instances from the Application Observability service.
The service count shown is lower than 4.
The service count shown is lower than 6.

questions.explanation: The Impact section is your blast radius summary. Always check it first to understand scope before diving into root cause analysis.
hints: Look at the Impact section tabs — the number in brackets next to 'Services' is your answer.

questions.title: Choosing your next step
questions.content: You want to understand the chain of service calls that led to this failure. Which built-in feature on the problem card would you use?

options.explanation: The Deployment tab shows deployment events, not service call chains.
Correct. The Visual resolution path renders a live topology map of all entities involved — showing which service called which, and where the problem propagated from.
Comments and insights is a collaboration feature, not an investigation tool.
Business flows shows end-to-end user journeys, not the service-level call chain.

questions.explanation: The Visual resolution path is the fastest way to see entity relationships and call chains during an incident. It shows you how the problem propagated across services.
hints: Look at the right-hand side of the problem card for a panel that shows a topology map of connected services.

learningObjectives: Identify the root cause entity from a Davis AI problem card
Read blast radius from the Impact section
Distinguish between event types (Slowdown vs Error) in the root cause panel
Use the Visual resolution path to understand service call chains
Interpret problem duration and severity from the problem header
